The seasons on Earth are caused by the tilt of the Earth's rotational axis relative to its orbital plane. This tilt, combined with the Earth's orbit around the Sun, results in the changing of the Sun's position in the sky throughout the year. This causes the Sun to appear higher in the sky during the summer months and lower during the winter months. As a result, the Sun's rays are more direct during the summer and less direct during the winter. This difference in the amount of direct sunlight can cause a change in the amount of daylight and the amount of daylight that can be used to produce energy.
